content.title: CHOOSING YOUR HERO
content.body:
Each player chooses one Hero to play. For this Adventure, the Party will use the following Heroes and Dungeon Roles:

  • Vorn — Defender: protects allies and holds the frontline.
  • Lorelai — Controller: moves enemies and creates openings.
  • Jaheen — Support: heals, protects, and removes harmful effects.
  • Maya — Striker: focuses on damage and priority targets.
  • Elros — Leader: coordinates the Party and enhances his allies.

Choose the Hero that best matches how you want to play.

For this Start Here walkthrough, make sure one player chooses Vorn. The guided first turn uses Vorn as the example Hero, while the remaining players may choose any other Heroes.

Use the full side of the Hero Board, as shown below:

Gather Your Hero Components

After choosing your Hero, take all components associated with that Hero:

  • Hero Board
  • Hero Card
  • Equipment cards
  • Dungeon Role Skill cards
  • Hero Skill cards
  • Class Ability cards
  • Starting Action Cubes

Each Hero has 2 Dungeon Role cards. These cards are part of the Hero’s basic setup and are used from the beginning of the Adventure.

When you choose your Hero, take the 2 Dungeon Role cards listed in that Hero’s section.

Your Hero Skill cards and Class Ability cards should be kept near your Hero Board, but they are not available yet. You will unlock them as your Hero progresses during the Adventure.

When you unlock a Hero Skill, you will also gain the Action Cube associated with that Skill.

content.title: VORN – FRONTLINE DEFENDER
content.body:
Vorn protects the Party by standing between his allies and danger. He can gain Shield, prevent damage, and keep enemies focused on him.

For this Adventure, Vorn uses the Defender Dungeon Role.

Core Components

Take Vorn's:

  • Hero Board
  • Hero Card
  • Starting Equipment cards
  • Starting Action Cubes

Dungeon Role Skills

Take the 2 Defender Dungeon Role cards.

Note: the Defender Role card has a Passive Ability that increases the Hero’s maximum health by 4. Adjust Vorn’s Health accordingly (16).

Progress Cards

Take all of Vorn’s Hero Skill cards and Class Ability cards and keep them near his Hero Board.

These cards are not available yet. You will unlock them as you progress during the Adventure.

content.title: PLAYER GIFTS
content.body:
For this Adventure, the Party receives a shared Gift Equipment Pack. Each Hero may choose 1 Gift Equipment card from this pack and equip it to the appropriate slot.

Remember to check your Hero’s Proficiency at the bottom of the Hero Board before equipping a card.

The Gift Equipment card used by each Hero during the Adventure becomes that player’s reward for participating and can be kept after the event.

Gift Equipment cards are available while supplies last. Ask the Store Owner for availability.

For your first game, we recommend the following Gift Equipment for each Hero:

  • Vorn: Bulwark Shield — This Shield gives you another way to Prevent damage for yourself or a teammate.
  • Lorelai: Bauble of Power — This Trinket gives your magic Skills an incremental damage bonus.
  • Jaheen: Heroic Heart — This Trinket improves your Cleanse effects, making you more effective as the Party’s Support.
  • Maya: Weakening Dagger — This Dagger gives you some protection and another chance to trigger your Passive Skill, Best Friends.
  • Elros: Boots of Haste – These Boots help you reach advantageous positions or make an extra attack to catch your foes by surprise.

content.title: FIRST ROOM SETUP
content.body:
Finishing the Setup

Place each Hero you are using on the Initiative Track according to their Dungeon Role. Then, place the Game Mechanic card “End of the Round” on the Rune Slot.

Next, prepare the First Room.

The Room Setup shows the starting positions for all Heroes, Monsters, and Objects in the First Room.

Use the legend to place each component:

  • Each icon shows the exact space where that token or miniature must be placed.
  • The labels "2+," "3+," and "4+" indicate how many Heroes must be in the Party for that element to be used. This means that elements with “3+”, for example, will only be placed if there are 3 or more Heroes in the Party.

In Drunagor Nights, some setup instructions refer to White, Gray, or Black Monsters. These labels indicate the type of Monster to be used for that Adventure.

For this First Room, place each Hero in the “Hero Starting Position” Squares, starting with Vorn on the left and the other Heroes in each Square to the right. The Heroes do not use snaps for their miniatures.

Use the specific Monsters listed below so the Start Here examples are easier to follow:

  • White Monster: Dead Marksman - Rookie
  • Gray Monster: Dire Headhunter - Rookie

In later rooms, when the Adventure asks you to place White, Gray, or Black Monsters, you may either choose Monsters of the indicated type or randomize them from the available Monsters.

Set up the room according to the number of Heroes in the Party:

  • 2 Heroes: Place the Heroes, 2 Chest tokens, 1 Dire Headhunters, and 2 Dead Marksman.
  • 3 Heroes: Add 1 Dire Headhunter in its marked position.
  • 4 Heroes: Add 1 Dire Headhunter and 1 Dead Marksman in their marked positions.

Monster Identification

For this First Room:

  • Use the first Monster Board (Yellow to Black) to track the Dead Marksmen and Dire Headhunters.
  • Attach the Yellow, Dark Blue, and Pink snaps, to the Dire Headhunters according to the number of Heroes in play.
  • Attach the Green, Red, and Black snaps, to the Dead Marksmen according to the number of Heroes in play.
  • Then place all Monsters on their indicated spaces on the map.

Now, take a moment to look at a Monster card.

Monster cards contain all the information needed to control enemy behavior during the Adventure.

For now, focus on these important sections:

  • Type — Indicates which type of Monster should be used during setup.
  • Rune Position — Shows where to place the card on the Initiative Track.
  • Health — Starting Health Points for that Monster.
  • Target Priority — Indicates how the Monster chooses its target.
  • Movement — How many Squares the Monster moves when activated.
  • Damage — Damage dealt when the Monster attacks.

The remaining information will become easier to understand as you continue playing.

Now, place a White Cube on the Monster Board to track each Monster's Health Points. Use the track that matches the color of that Monster's snap.

Each Monster's starting Health is shown on its Monster card. If a Monster gains a Condition during the Adventure, place the corresponding Condition token on the matching track of the Monster Board.

content.title: INITIATIVE TRACK
content.body:
Place the Monster cards on the Initiative Track according to the Rune shown on each card.

Normally, Monster cards, Minion cards, and Boss or Commander Attack cards are placed above or below the matching Rune on the Initiative Track. Heroes are placed above or below their Dungeon Roles.

content.title: YOUR FIRST TURN
content.body:
Now that everything is ready, it's time to begin the Adventure.

The following example demonstrates the basic flow of a round and introduces the core mechanics of play. After completing this walkthrough, you may continue the Adventure from that point or restart the round and play it again.

The Initiative Track shows that Vorn is the first Hero to act.

At the start of his turn, Vorn checks whether he is affected by any Conditions. He is not, so he proceeds to the Take Actions step. This means he can take two Cube Actions, up to one Minor Action, and has a Free Movement.

First, Vorn will use his Minor Action for the turn to Loot the Chest in front of him. He draws a Chest card, placing it on one of his bag slots, below his Player board. Then, he removes the Chest token from the map. He can later discard this card to use its effects. As part of the same Minor Action, Vorn could use the Item immediately or give it to another Hero at Any Range, but he chooses to keep the item for now.

For his first Cube Action, Vorn takes a Red Action Cube and places it on his Hammer Throw Skill.

Resolve the first effect of the Skill: Self: Shield 2. Vorn gains 2 Shield tokens.

Rule Tip — Shield: Each Shield token prevents 1 damage. Stackable tokens, such as Shield, have a maximum of 4 tokens.

Next, resolve the damage effect, represented by the ¹ icon. Hammer Throw deals 3 Damage to a target within range. Since Vorn used a Red Action Cube, the range is 1 Area.

The only enemy within range is the Red Dire Headhunter, so Vorn chooses it as the target and records 3 Damage on the Monster Board.

Now Vorn uses his Free Movement, repositioning himself in front of the Dire Headhunter.

For his second Cube Action, Vorn uses a Yellow Action Cube and places it on his Guarding Blow Melee Skill.

First, resolve the Skill’s Shield effect. Vorn may choose a target within Melee Range to gain Shield 2. He chooses one of his adjacent allies, who gains 2 Shield tokens.

Next, resolve the attack effect. When making a ², the Hero rolls a D20, adds any bonuses they have, and compares the result to their weapon Accuracy Value. If the final number is equal to or higher than the Accuracy Value, the attack hits.

Tutorial Note: When rolling an Attack, if the roll is a natural 20, it’s a Critical Hit, meaning it deals double the attack’s damage. If it’s a natural 1, it’s a Critical Miss, meaning the attack fails regardless of bonuses. “Natural” refers to the value rolled on the D20, ignoring any bonuses or penalties.

Guarding Blow allows Vorn to make an attack roll with +5 to Hit, meaning he gets an +5 bonus to his attack roll.

Roll a D20 and add +5 to the result.

For this example, assume the attack is successful.

Vorn deals damage equal to his weapon Damage Attribute, which is 3 Damage, to the Dire Headhunter. Record this damage on the Monster Board.

Tutorial Note: The Dire Headhunter has the “Counter 2” ability. The blue color indicates that it’s a triggered ability. In this case, the Monster causes 2 damage to each Hero adjacent to it whenever a Hero misses an Attack against it.

After resolving all of his actions, Vorn ends his turn.

content.title: MONSTERS’ TURN
content.body:
After each Character’s turn, the Initiative Marker moves to the next Character in order, from left to right on the top row, then left to right on the bottom row.

The next Character on the Initiative Track is the Dead Marksmen.

When activating Monsters, resolve them one at a time, following the color order shown on the Monster Board.

The first Monster to activate is the Green Dead Marksman.

Looking at the Dead Marksman card, we can see that its target priority is Strongest Hero. This means it will target the Hero with the highest current Health Points among those it can reach.

In this situation, that Hero is Vorn.

First, the Dead Marksman attempts to move into range of its target.

It needs to move 3 Squares to reach Range 1 of Vorn. Once in range, it attacks and deals 6 Damage.

Before the damage is applied, the Heroes have an opportunity to use Reactions.

To resolve the attack, first remove Vorn’s 2 Shield tokens. Each Shield token prevents 1 Damage, so 4 Damage remain.

Each Hero may use 1 Reaction for each Hero being attacked.

Jaheen decides to react by using his Intervention Skill, which prevents 3 Damage.

After Shield and Prevention are applied, Vorn takes 1 Damage.

Since Vorn lost Health from the attack, he also suffers the Monster’s Collateral Damage and receives 2 Poison tokens. Collateral Damage abilities in Monsters written in black, and are applied if the Target loses any Health from this Monster’s Attack. If all Damage had been prevented, Vorn would not suffer the Collateral Damage.

Rule Tip — Poison: Poison deals damage to a Hero at the start of each of their turns. Vorn has 2 Poison tokens, so he will take 2 Damage at the start of each of his turns until the Poison is removed.

If Jaheen is not in the Party, Vorn can instead use his Parry Skill as a Reaction, preventing 3 Damage himself.

Tutorial Note: Vorn could also use his Parry Skill as a Reaction, in addition to Jaheen’s Intervention, to prevent the remaining Damage. This example does not use Parry so it can demonstrate how Collateral Damage and Poison work. If Jaheen is not in the Party, use Vorn’s Parry, using a Green Cube.

This concludes the activation of the first Dead Marksman.

Following the color order on the Monster Board, the next Monster to activate is the Red Dead Marksman. Its target is again the Strongest Hero, which is still Vorn.

It moves up to its full Movement value of 3 Squares toward Vorn, but this is not enough to reach Range 1. Since it cannot get within range, it ends its activation without attacking.

The same happens with the Black Dead Marksman: it moves as close as possible to Vorn, then ends its activation because it is still unable to attack.

This concludes the Dead Marksmen's activation.

The round now proceeds to the next Character on the Initiative Track.

content.title: OTHER IMPORTANT RULES
content.body:
Before you continue, review these short reminders. You do not need to memorize them now, but they may come up during the Adventure.

Rune Cards

A Rune card is already placed on the Initiative Track during setup. When the Initiative Marker reaches a Rune card, pause and follow the instructions on that card.

Rune cards introduce Adventure mechanics that are active at that moment, such as events, hazards, objectives, or special effects.

Action Cube Ranges

Curse Cubes

Curse Cubes represent the physical, spiritual, and mental exhaustion suffered by the Heroes. Unlike Action Cubes, Curse Cubes are harmful.

Curse Cubes are Black cubes. When a Hero gains a Curse Cube, assign it to one of that Hero’s Hero Skills or Dungeon Role Skills.

A Skill with a Curse Cube assigned to it is blocked and cannot be used until the Curse Cube is removed by a Cleanse effect.

If a Hero has 6 Curse Cubes on their board at the same time, that Hero is defeated and the Adventure immediately fails.

Recall Action

As Heroes use Skills, their Action Cube Reserve will eventually run low. A Recall Action lets you return all spent and Expended Action Cubes to your Reserve.

There are two types of Recall:

  • Willing Recall: At the end of your turn, if you have Action Cubes of 2 or fewer colors in your Reserve, you may Recall. If you do, your turn ends immediately.
  • Unwilling Recall: If you spend or Expend your last Action Cube and your Reserve becomes empty, you must Recall immediately. This can happen during or outside your turn, and it does not end the turn.

Whenever you perform a Recall, whether Willing or Unwilling, you suffer a Recall penalty: gain 1 Curse Cube and assign it to one of your Hero Skills or Dungeon Role Skills.

Knockout

When a Hero’s Health is reduced to 0 or less, that Hero is Knocked Out.

Place their model lying down on the board, then:

  • Remove all Conditions from that Hero.
  • Recall all of their Action Cubes.
  • Assign 1 Trauma Cube to one of their Hero Skills or Dungeon Role Skills.

While Knocked Out, a Hero cannot act, use Skills, be targeted, take Damage, or receive Conditions.

At the beginning of that Hero’s next turn, stand their model back up and restore their Health to the maximum. Beginning of Turn Skills work normally on that turn.

Combat Engagement

Neither Heroes nor Enemies can make ranged Attacks while adjacent to an Enemy. This is called Combat Engagement. Enemies move away from Heroes if needed for them to Attack. If they can’t reach any Square where they will not be adjacent to a Hero, they do not move and don’t Attack that turn. For Hero Skills, Combat Engagement only applies to Attacks ², but not for other effects like ¹.

Hero Progression

During the Adventure, your Hero will learn new Hero Skills and Class Abilities.

When your Hero learns a Level 1 Hero Skill, take the chosen Hero Skill card and 1 Action Cube of the matching color. Place both on your Hero Board.

When your Hero learns a Level 2 Hero Skill, flip that same Hero Skill card so both Skills are available. Then, take 1 additional Action Cube of the matching color and add it to your Hero Board.

A Hero cannot learn a Level 2 Hero Skill before learning the Level 1 Skill from the same card.

When your Hero learns a Class Ability, place the chosen Class Ability card next to your Hero Board. Then, take 1 White Cube and place it in the matching slot to mark the ability you learned.

A Hero cannot learn a Level 2 or Level 3 Class Ability before learning the previous ability from the same card.

Defeating Monsters

When a Monster's Health is reduced to 0 or less, it is defeated.

Remove its miniature from the map and remove its Health marker from the Monster Board. Any Conditions affecting that Monster are also removed.

Defeated Monsters no longer activate or affect the Adventure.

content.title: ADVENTURE RULES
content.body:
Before you continue, review the special rules that are active during this Adventure.

Defeat Conditions

The Adventure immediately fails if any of the following happens:

  • A Rune cannot be drawn from the bag.
  • Any Hero has 2 Trauma Cubes on their board at the same time.
  • Any Hero has 6 Curse Cubes on their board at the same time.

If any Hero is defeated, the Party cannot proceed.

Stirring Darkness

The Darkness is especially strong here.

There are only 12 Runes in the Rune bag. This is enough for 9 complete rounds before the Party risks failing to draw a Rune.

Plan your actions carefully and do not let the Adventure drag on for too long.

Continue the Adventure

This concludes this Start Here guide. Now, you can choose either to restart the Adventure or continue playing from the next character’s turn. If you have any questions regarding Keywords or the mechanics of the turn, feel free to check the Player Aid or the Keyword tab on the Drunagor App.

content.title: OPENING A DOOR
content.body:
1. ## Opening a Door

Each Door in Drunagor is divided in 3 sections:

Whenever you open a new Door, you will find three types of information.

First, the Narrative Section, which describes what your Heroes encounter as they move deeper into the Adventure.

Next, the Setup Section, showing the map layout, which components are needed, and where each element must be placed.

Finally, the Special Rules Section. This section may introduce new room effects, temporary game mechanics, Hero Progression, Scene instructions, or other special events that affect the Adventure.

2. ## Building the Setup

You will use three different types of Dungeon Trays during the game. Each Tray is shaped to fit specific map configurations.
To make setup easier, each Map Tile shows a map code and a box symbol to help you identify it.

Using the Setup as a reference, place the Map Tiles in their shown positions.

3. ## Place Tokens and Door

Each Setup shows exactly which Tokens to use, as well as how many and where to place them.

Using the Setup as a guide, place the corresponding Tokens and the next Door in their shown positions.

4. ## Prepare and Place the Monsters

As in the First Room, prepare the Monsters for this new area.

From this Room onward, you will randomize the Monsters according to the Monster types shown in the Setup.

Then, place the Monster cards on the Initiative Track, set their Health on the Monster Board, and place the miniatures on the map.

5. ## Special Rules

Read and follow the instructions shown on the right side of the Door.

This section includes Hero Progression, special mechanics, and other instructions that become active during the Adventure.

Resolve all instructions shown here before continuing.
